claim: Anatomical models of memory over the last 50 years have repeatedly highlighted the hippocampal inputs to the mammillary bodies via the postcommissural fornix.
source_text: Over the last 50 years, anatomical models of memory have repeatedly highlighted the hippocampal inputs to the mammillary bodies via the postcommissural fornix.
evidence_reasoning: This claim references established historical models in the field and is supported by citations to prior work (e.g., Papez, 1937; Barbizet, 1963; Delay and Brion, 1969).

claim: Anatomical models of memory downplay other projections to the mammillary bodies, leaving them largely ignored.
source_text: Such models downplay other projections to the mammillary bodies, leaving them largely ignored.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the historical focus on hippocampal inputs and the lack of attention to other pathways in previous models.

claim: Only mammillothalamic tract and Gudden's ventral tegmental nucleus lesions impaired behavioral tests of spatial working memory.
source_text: Only mammillothalamic tract and Gudden's ventral tegmental nucleus lesions impaired behavioral tests of spatial working memory and, in particular, disrupted the use of extramaze spatial landmarks.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by experimental data from behavioral testing reported in the manuscript.

claim: Mammillothalamic tract and Gudden's ventral tegmental nucleus lesions disrupted the use of extramaze spatial landmarks.
source_text: Only mammillothalamic tract and Gudden's ventral tegmental nucleus lesions impaired behavioral tests of spatial working memory and, in particular, disrupted the use of extramaze spatial landmarks.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by experimental observations from the behavioral tasks described in the manuscript.

claim: Mammillothalamic tract and Gudden's ventral tegmental nucleus lesions produced widespread reductions in immediate-early gene (c-fos) expression in a network of memory-related regions.
source_text: The same lesions also produced widespread reductions in immediate-early gene (c- fos ) expression in a network of memory-related regions, not seen after postcommissural fornix lesions.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by immunohistochemical data presented in Experiment 4.

claim: Postcommissural fornix lesions did not produce widespread reductions in c-fos expression in memory-related regions.
source_text: The same lesions also produced widespread reductions in immediate-early gene (c- fos ) expression in a network of memory-related regions, not seen after postcommissural fornix lesions.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the c-fos expression data showing no significant reductions in the PCFx group.

claim: The findings are inconsistent with previous models of mammillary body function dominated by hippocampal inputs.
source_text: These findings are inconsistent with previous models of mammillary body function (those dominated by hippocampal inputs) and herald a new understanding of why specific diencephalic structures are vital for memory.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the experimental data showing that hippocampal disconnection (PCFx) did not impair memory while VTNx lesions did.

claim: The mammillary bodies are principally seen as a relay of hippocampal projections to the anterior thalamic nuclei.
source_text: Consequently, the mammillary bodies are principally seen as a relay of hippocampal projections to the anterior thalamic nuclei and, from there, to the cingulate (Barbizet, 1963; Delay and Brion, 1969) and prefrontal (Warrington and Weiskrantz, 1982) cortices.
evidence_reasoning: This represents the established view in the field, supported by multiple citations.

claim: The hippocampal projections to the mammillary bodies are unidirectional.
source_text: The notion that the mammillary bodies form part of such an 'extended hippocampal system' (Aggleton and Brown, 1999) is seemingly supported by the unidirectional nature of the hippocampal projections to the mammillary bodies (Aggleton et al., 2005)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Aggleton et al., 2005 and represents established anatomical knowledge.

claim: The mammillary bodies receive dense inputs from Gudden's tegmental nuclei.
source_text: The mammillary bodies receive dense inputs from Gudden's tegmental nuclei (e.g., Takeuchi et al., 1985)
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by citation to Takeuchi et al., 1985.

claim: Standard models of mammillary body function provide no real function for the mammillary bodies.
source_text: However, these standard models suffer two major shortcomings. First, they provide no real function for the mammillary bodies and second, they ignore other mammillary body afferents.
evidence_reasoning: This is a critical assessment of existing models based on their conceptual limitations.

claim: Standard models of mammillary body function ignore other mammillary body afferents.
source_text: However, these standard models suffer two major shortcomings. First, they provide no real function for the mammillary bodies and second, they ignore other mammillary body afferents.
evidence_reasoning: This is a critical assessment based on review of existing literature and models.

claim: The ventral tegmental nucleus of Gudden is reciprocally connected with the medial mammillary nucleus.
source_text: The present study focused on the ventral tegmental nucleus of Gudden as it is reciprocally connected with the medial mammillary nucleus while the dorsal tegmental nucleus connects with the lateral mammillary nucleus.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established anatomical knowledge about connectivity patterns.

claim: The dorsal tegmental nucleus connects with the lateral mammillary nucleus.
source_text: The present study focused on the ventral tegmental nucleus of Gudden as it is reciprocally connected with the medial mammillary nucleus while the dorsal tegmental nucleus connects with the lateral mammillary nucleus.
evidence_reasoning: This represents established anatomical knowledge about connectivity patterns.

claim: Loss of the medial mammillary system is principally responsible for spatial memory impairments associated with complete lesions of the mammillary bodies.
source_text: Although the lateral mammillary nucleus forms part of the head-direction network (e.g., Vann and Aggleton, 2004; Hopkins, 2005), it is the loss of the medial mammillary system that appears principally responsible for the spatial memory impairments associated with complete lesions of this structure (Vann, 2005, 2010, 2011; Vann and Albasser, 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work by the authors and others.

claim: The medial mammillary nucleus is always atrophied in the amnesic Korsakoff's syndrome.
source_text: Furthermore, it is the medial mammillary nucleus that is always atrophied in the amnesic Korsakoff's syndrome (Victor et al., 1989; Kopelman, 1995).
evidence_reasoning: This clinical observation is supported by citations to Victor et al., 1989 and Kopelman, 1995.

claim: Postcommissural fornix lesions disconnect the hippocampal formation projections to the mammillary bodies whilst leaving other hippocampal connections intact.
source_text: In one group the descending postcommissural fornix (PCF) was lesioned, a procedure that disconnects the hippocampal formation projections to the mammillary bodies whilst leaving other hippocampal connections intact, including those with the septum, striatum and anterior thalamic nuclei (Vann et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Vann et al., 2011 and represents established anatomical knowledge about the effects of this lesion.

claim: Postcommissural fornix lesions leave hippocampal connections with the septum, striatum and anterior thalamic nuclei intact.
source_text: In one group the descending postcommissural fornix (PCF) was lesioned, a procedure that disconnects the hippocampal formation projections to the mammillary bodies whilst leaving other hippocampal connections intact, including those with the septum, striatum and anterior thalamic nuclei (Vann et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by citation to Vann et al., 2011.

claim: T-maze alternation is sensitive to hippocampal damage.
source_text: Rats were tested on three behavioral tasks, the first two of which are sensitive to hippocampal damage: T-maze alternation, a working memory task in the radial-arm maze, and a geometric discrimination task (Aggleton et al., 2009; Vann, 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous work showing hippocampal sensitivity of these tasks.

claim: The radial-arm maze working memory task is sensitive to hippocampal damage.
source_text: Rats were tested on three behavioral tasks, the first two of which are sensitive to hippocampal damage: T-maze alternation, a working memory task in the radial-arm maze, and a geometric discrimination task (Aggleton et al., 2009; Vann, 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to previous work showing hippocampal sensitivity of these tasks.

claim: MTT lesions result in widespread neural hypoactivity as measured by expression of the immediate-early gene c-fos.
source_text: In addition to impairing spatial memory, MTT lesions also result in widespread neural hypoactivity, as measured by expression of the immediate-early gene c-fos (Vann and Albasser, 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Vann and Albasser, 2009.

claim: The final study groups comprised seven Gudden's ventral tegmental nuclei lesion animals, eight mammillothalamic tract lesion animals, seven postcommissural fornix lesions, and eight surgical controls.
source_text: A stringent lesion criterion was adopted for final inclusion in the study and, as a consequence, the final groups comprised seven Gudden's ventral tegmental nuclei lesion animals (VTNx), eight mammillothalamic tract lesion animals (MTTx), seven postcommissural fornix lesions (PCFx) and eight surgical controls (Sham).
evidence_reasoning: This reports the actual group sizes used in the study after applying inclusion criteria.

claim: The laterodorsal tegmental nucleus is the sole source of anterior thalamic cholinergic innervations.
source_text: The integrity of the laterodorsal tegmental nucleus is important, being the sole source of anterior thalamic cholinergic innervations and a major source of interpeduncular cholinergic inputs (Satoh and Fibiger, 1986; Sikes and Vogt, 1987).
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by citations to Satoh and Fibiger, 1986 and Sikes and Vogt, 1987.

claim: The laterodorsal tegmental nucleus is a major source of interpeduncular cholinergic inputs.
source_text: The integrity of the laterodorsal tegmental nucleus is important, being the sole source of anterior thalamic cholinergic innervations and a major source of interpeduncular cholinergic inputs (Satoh and Fibiger, 1986; Sikes and Vogt, 1987).
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by citations to Satoh and Fibiger, 1986 and Sikes and Vogt, 1987.

claim: The laterodorsal tegmental nuclei and their cholinergic projections were intact in VTNx animals.
source_text: The observation that the laterodorsal tegmental nuclei, and subsequently their cholinergic projections, were intact was confirmed by assessing the level of acetylcholinesterase staining in the anteroventral thalamic nucleus (Figure 1C,D) and interpeduncular nucleus.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by acetylcholinesterase staining data showing no difference between VTNx and Sham groups.

claim: Fornix section leads to shrinkage of the mammillary bodies due to loss of white matter.
source_text: It has been repeatedly shown that fornix section leads to shrinkage of the mammillary bodies (due to loss of white matter).
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: The mean mammillary body area for the PCFx group (1.34 mm²) was significantly smaller than the Sham group (1.79 mm²).
source_text: The mean mammillary body area (±SEM) for the PCFx group was 1.34 mm2 ± 0.031, making them significantly smaller than the Sham group measurements of 1.79 mm2 ± 0.058 (t(13) = 6.44; p<0.001; Figure 1G,H).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by quantitative measurements and statistical analysis.

claim: The reduced mammillary body volumes of the PCFx lesion cohort did not differ from a previous cohort where retrograde tracers confirmed postcommissural fornix disconnection.
source_text: Furthermore, the reduced mammillary body volumes of the present PCFx lesion cohort did not differ from a previous cohort where retrograde tracers had been used to confirm the postcommissural fornix disconnection (t(14)=1.67; p>0.1)
evidence_reasoning: This comparison with previous validated lesions provides evidence for the completeness of the current lesions.

claim: The reduced mammillary body volume in the PCFx group reflects loss of white matter and not an overall change in neuronal numbers.
source_text: This is consistent with the reduced mammillary body volume in the PCFx group reflecting loss of white matter and not an overall change in neuronal numbers (Figure 1I,J).
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from cell packing density data showing increased packing in PCFx but not other groups.

claim: Cell packing in the PCFx lesion group was significantly increased compared to all three other groups.
source_text: There was an overall group effect (F(3,27) = 9.96, p<0.001) which reflected a significant increase in the cell packing in the PCFx lesion group compared to all three other groups (Sham, p<0.01; MTTx, p<0.005; VTNx, p<0.001)
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by quantitative cell counting data and statistical analysis.

claim: Lack of difference in cell packing in the MTTx and VTNx groups, combined with reduced cross-sectional area, is consistent with some medial mammillary body cell loss in these groups.
source_text: In contrast, lack of difference in cell packing in the MTTx and VTNx groups, combined with reduced cross-sectional area, would be consistent with some medial mammillary body cell loss in these groups.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the combination of reduced area without increased cell packing density.

claim: Rats can use multiple cue-types to perform spatial alternation tasks.
source_text: Rats can use multiple cue-types to perform spatial alternation tasks
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as established knowledge about rat spatial behavior.

claim: In Stage 1 of T-maze alternation, there was an overall effect of lesion.
source_text: There was an overall effect of lesion (F(3,27) = 4.93, p=0.007; Figure 2B)
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis of behavioral data.

claim: The performance of the VTNx group in Stage 1 was significantly worse than the Sham group.
source_text: Post-hoc analyses revealed the performance of the VTNx group to be significantly worse than the Sham group (p=0.005).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by post-hoc statistical analysis of behavioral data.

claim: In Stage 2 of T-maze alternation, the performances of both the MTTx and VTNx groups were significantly worse than the Sham rats.
source_text: The group effect reflected the lower scores of both the MTTx (p=0.004) and VTNx (p=0.006) groups compared to the Sham rats.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis of behavioral data from Stage 2.

claim: The lack of impairment in the MTTx group in Stage 1 reflected their use of intra-maze cues.
source_text: These results suggest that the lack of impairment in the MTTx group in Stage 1 reflected their use of intra-maze cues, such as odor trails.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the pattern of impairment appearing only when intra-maze cues were removed in Stage 2.

claim: Same place trials were more difficult than different place trials in Stage 2.
source_text: Overall, same place trials were more difficult than different place trials (F(1,27) = 25.4, p<0.001)
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis of trial type effects.

claim: Previous studies have shown that rats find it very difficult to use egocentric cues for delayed alternation.
source_text: While both direction cues and egocentric cues were available during this stage, previous studies have shown that rats find it very difficult to use egocentric cues (e.g., body turns) for delayed alternation (Baird et al., 2004; Futter and Aggleton, 2006; Pothuizen et al., 2008)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to previous behavioral studies.

claim: In Stage 3, the performances of the VTNx and MTTx groups were significantly worse than those of both the Sham group and the PCFx group.
source_text: Post-hoc analyses revealed that the performances of the VTNx and MTTx groups were significantly worse than those of both the Sham group (VTNx, p=0.025; MTTx, p=0.019) and the PCFx group (VTNx, p=0.029; MTTx, p=0.023).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by post-hoc statistical analysis of Stage 3 behavioral data.

claim: During radial-arm maze acquisition, all groups showed an improvement across training.
source_text: Although all groups showed an improvement across training, it appears that in the VTNx and MTTx groups this reflected a greater reliance on the use of intra-maze cues given the disruptive effect of rotating the maze midway through the trial.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by behavioral data showing improvement during acquisition but impairment when the maze was rotated.

claim: Following maze rotation, the MTTx and VTNx groups made significantly more errors than the Sham group.
source_text: Following this manipulation the groups significantly differed in terms of number of errors made (F(3,27) = 6.35, p=0.002; Figure 3A) and correct entries in the first eight choices (F(3,27) = 6.80, p=0.001; Figure 3B). Post-hoc comparisons revealed this group effect to be due to differences between the Sham group and both the MTTx (errors, p=0.007; entries, p=0.015) and VTNx groups (errors, p=0.023; entries, p=0.022).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis of behavioral data from the rotation stage.

claim: Both behavioral tasks indicated that the MTTx and VTNx rats were less able to use allocentric cues and more reliant on intra-maze cues.
source_text: Thus both behavioral tasks indicated that the MTTx and VTNx rats were less able to use allocentric cues and more reliant on intra-maze cues.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the pattern of impairments across both T-maze and radial-arm maze tasks.

claim: The PCFx animals were not impaired relative to the Shams on any of the behavioral tasks.
source_text: In contrast, the PCFx animals were not impaired relative to the Shams on any of the behavioral tasks.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the absence of significant differences in all behavioral comparisons.

claim: The PCFx animals performed significantly better than both the VTNx and MTTx groups on both the radial-arm maze and T-maze tasks.
source_text: Consequently, the PCFx animals performed significantly better than both the VTNx and MTTx groups on both the radial-arm maze and T-maze tasks despite producing MB shrinkage (resulting from loss of fiber inputs) equivalent to that found after complete fornix lesions.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by post-hoc statistical comparisons showing significant differences.

claim: The present PCFx lesions were indistinguishable from those that had previously been demonstrated to completely disconnect the hippocampal formation-MB projections.
source_text: The present PCFx lesions were indistinguishable from those that had previously been demonstrated to completely disconnect the hippocampal formation-MB projections (Vann et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by comparison with previous validated lesions and citation to Vann et al., 2011.

claim: Both the VTNx and MTTx groups had significantly fewer c-Fos positive cells in the hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, and prelimbic cortex.
source_text: The pattern of behavioral impairments was paralleled by the c-Fos findings. Both the VTNx and MTTx groups had significantly fewer c-Fos positive cells in the hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, and prelimbic cortex.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by c-Fos immunohistochemistry data and statistical analysis.

claim: Reduced levels of c-Fos have been found in the same network of brain regions following anterior thalamic nuclei lesions.
source_text: Reduced levels of c-Fos have also been found in this same network of brain regions following anterior thalamic nuclei lesions (Jenkins et al., 2002).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Jenkins et al., 2002.

claim: The MTT and VTNg lesions do not result in direct de-afferentation of the hippocampus, retrosplenial cortex, or prelimbic cortex.
source_text: However, unlike the c-Fos reduction following anterior thalamic lesions, the current changes reflect 'indirect' effects, as the MTT and VTNg lesions do not result in direct de-afferentation of any of these sites.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from anatomical knowledge about the connectivity of these structures.

claim: Reduced activity in memory-related networks is a consistent marker of damage to the medial diencephalon in animal models and humans.
source_text: Although reduced activity in this memory-related network seems to be a consistent marker of damage to the medial diencephalon, in animal models and humans (Joyce et al., 1994; Kapur, 1994; Reed et al., 2003; Savage et al., 2003; Caulo et al., 2005; Anzalone et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to studies in both animals and humans.

claim: Learning and memory deficits are found after infusions of antisense that block c-Fos activity.
source_text: Evidence for the former account comes learning and memory deficits found after infusions of antisense that block c-Fos activity (He et al., 2002; Seoane et al., 2012; Katche et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to He et al., 2002; Seoane et al., 2012; Katche et al., 2013.

claim: The present PCFx lesion findings were remarkably similar to those found previously, resulting in a 5% reduction in accuracy of T-maze alternation.
source_text: The present PCFx lesion findings were remarkably similar to those found previously (Vann et al., 2011), for example, they resulted in a 5% reduction in accuracy of T-maze alternation.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by comparison with previous findings and citation to Vann et al., 2011.

claim: The hippocampal projections to the MBs and anterior thalamic nuclei arise from different cell populations.
source_text: The hippocampal projections to the MBs and anterior thalamic nuclei arise from different cell populations (Wright et al., 2010)
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical fact is supported by citation to Wright et al., 2010.

claim: VTNg cells fire rhythmically and coherently with hippocampal theta.
source_text: VTNg cells fire rhythmically and coherently with hippocampal theta (Kocsis et al., 2001)
evidence_reasoning: This physiological property is supported by citation to Kocsis et al., 2001.

claim: Theta-related cells in the medial mammillary nucleus have been linked to memory function.
source_text: and theta-related cells in the medial mammillary nucleus have been linked to memory function (Alonso and Llinas, 1992; Kocsis and Vertes, 1994; Bland et al., 1995; Kirk et al., 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations linking theta activity to memory.

claim: The VTNg has been linked to vigilance states.
source_text: It is also the case that the VTNg have been linked to vigilance states (Bassant and Poindessous-Jazat, 2001)
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Bassant and Poindessous-Jazat, 2001.

claim: The VTNg innervates the lateral hypothalamus, preoptic area, medial septum, parts of the reticular pontine nucleus, median raphe nuclei, supramammillary nucleus and ventral tegmental area.
source_text: The VTNg does, however, innervate a number of other sites, including the lateral hypothalamus, preoptic area, medial septum, parts of the reticular pontine nucleus, median raphe nuclei, supramammillary nucleus and ventral tegmental area (Petrovicky, 1973; Leichnetz et al., 1989; Hayakawa et al., 1993).
evidence_reasoning: This anatomical connectivity is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The lack of Fos changes in the supramammillary and septal nuclei following VTNg lesions provides evidence that VTNg effects are not via these routes.
source_text: In addition, the lack of Fos changes in the supramammillary and septal nuclei following VTNg lesions provides some evidence that they are not having their effects via these routes
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the c-Fos data showing no changes in these regions.

claim: The MTT and VTNg lesion effects appear to be selective for spatial working memory and not due to non-specific effects such as loss of arousal or motivation.
source_text: In rats, the MTT and VTNg lesion effects appear to be selective for spatial working memory and not due to non-specific effects such as loss of arousal or motivation.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the selective pattern of impairments across different task types.

claim: Both MTTx and VTNx groups were able to acquire a geometric discrimination task at the same rate, and to the same level, as the Sham group.
source_text: Both MTTx and VTNx groups were able to acquire a geometric discrimination task at the same rate, and to the same level, as the Sham group.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by behavioral data from the geometric discrimination task.

claim: The geometric discrimination task may be particularly sensitive to lesions within the head-direction system.
source_text: This task may be particularly sensitive to lesions within the head-direction system (Aggleton et al., 2009; Vann, 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Aggleton et al., 2009 and Vann, 2011.

claim: The MTT lesions in the present study are most likely to disconnect the medial MB efferents, while leaving many lateral MB efferents largely intact.
source_text: As the MTT lesions in the present study are most likely to disconnect the medial MB efferents, while leaving many lateral MB efferents largely intact (Vann and Albasser, 2009)
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from anatomical knowledge and supported by citation to Vann and Albasser, 2009.

claim: Clinical studies show that both the MBs and the MTT are important for human memory, and recollective memory in particular.
source_text: Clinical studies show that both the MBs and the MTT are important for human memory, and recollective memory in particular (Dusoir et al., 1990; Van der Werf et al., 2000; Carlesimo et al., 2007; Tsivilis et al., 2008; Vann et al., 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to clinical studies.

claim: For a number of years the very existence of the VTNg in humans had been in doubt.
source_text: Indeed, for a number of years the very existence of this nucleus in humans had been in doubt (Petrovicky, 1971; Hayakawa and Zyo, 1983).
evidence_reasoning: This historical fact is supported by citations to Petrovicky, 1971 and Hayakawa and Zyo, 1983.

claim: The structure and connections of the VTNg are remarkably similar across species.
source_text: However, it is now apparent that the structure and connections of the VTNg are remarkably similar across species (Petrovicky, 1973; Irle and Markowitsch, 1982; Hayakawa and Zyo, 1984; Huang et al., 1992; Saunders et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to comparative anatomical studies.

claim: There is only one reported amnesic patient with restricted damage in the VTN area.
source_text: To date, there is only one reported amnesic patient with restricted damage in the VTN area, but this study is limited in that only CT images were available (Goldberg et al., 1981).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citation to Goldberg et al., 1981.

claim: The findings show that the MBs have important roles in memory that can be independent of their hippocampal inputs.
source_text: The current findings support a novel model of limbic brain interactions. They show that the MBs have important roles in memory that can be independent of their hippocampal inputs; instead, the results highlight the VTNg.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the pattern of behavioral and c-Fos results showing VTNx but not PCFx impairments.

claim: MTT and VTNg lesions result in strikingly similar spatial memory impairments.
source_text: Not only do MTT and VTNg lesions result in strikingly similar spatial memory impairments but they also both result in widespread hypoactivity across a memory-related network.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the behavioral and c-Fos data showing parallel effects of these two lesions.

claim: MTT and VTNg lesions both result in widespread hypoactivity across a memory-related network.
source_text: Not only do MTT and VTNg lesions result in strikingly similar spatial memory impairments but they also both result in widespread hypoactivity across a memory-related network.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by c-Fos expression data from multiple brain regions.

claim: In the retrosplenial cortex, c-Fos counts in the Sham group were significantly higher than both the MTTx and VTNx groups.
source_text: There was a significant group effect (F(3,26) = 6.52, p=0.002; Figure 5A) as c-Fos counts in the Sham group were significantly higher than both the MTTx (p=0.009) and VTNx groups (p=0.006).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by c-Fos counting data and statistical analysis.

claim: In the hippocampus, c-Fos counts in the Sham group were significantly higher than both the MTTx and VTNx groups.
source_text: There was a main group effect (F(3,26) = 5.52, p=0.05; Figure 5A) as c-Fos counts in the Sham group were significantly higher than both the MTTx group (p=0.029) and VTNx groups (p=0.009).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by c-Fos counting data and statistical analysis.

claim: The lesion-induced changes in hippocampal c-fos expression appeared to be largely driven by reductions in CA1.
source_text: These analyses revealed that the lesion-induced changes in hippocampual c-fos expression appeared to be largely driven by reductions in CA1 as this was the only subfield where there was a significant group difference
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from subfield-specific analysis showing significant effects only in CA1.

claim: In the prelimbic cortex, significantly fewer c-Fos positive cells were found in the MTTx and VTNx groups than in the Sham group.
source_text: In contrast, analyses of the prelimbic cortex revealed an overall group effect (F(3,26) = 5.32, p=0.006; Figure 5B) as significantly fewer c-Fos positive cells were found in the MTTx ( p=0.041) and VTNx (p=0.017) groups than in the Sham group.
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by c-Fos counting data and statistical analysis.

claim: There was no group effect for c-Fos expression in the infralimbic cortex.
source_text: There was no group effect when analysing the infralimbic cortex (F(3,26) =1.23, p>0.3; Figure 5B).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis showing no significant differences.

claim: There was no group effect for c-Fos expression in the somatosensory cortex, supramammillary nucleus, lateral septum, or medial septum.
source_text: There was no group effect for somatosensory cortex (F < 1; Figure 5C), supramammillary nucleus, lateral or medial septum (all F < 1; Figure 5C).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by statistical analysis showing no significant differences in these regions.

claim: On the final test day, all animals completed approximately four trials during the 20 min test session with no group difference in trial numbers.
source_text: On the final test day, when animals were tested in the novel room, all animals completed approximately four trials (a trial is completed when all eight arms have been visited) during the 20 min test session (trials completed: VTNx= 4.0 ± 0.0; MTTx = 4.0 ± 0.0; PCFx = 3.9 ± 0.1; Sham = 4.0 ± 0.1), with no group difference in trial numbers (F(3,27) = 1.85, p>0.1).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by behavioral data from the final test session.

claim: Peak levels of the Fos protein are found approximately 90 min after activation.
source_text: This time window was chosen as peak levels of the Fos protein are found approximately 90 min after activation (e.g., Sharp et al., 1993; Chaudhuri et al., 2000).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Sharp et al., 1993 and Chaudhuri et al., 2000.
